subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A lipid molecule is made up of:
options: One sugar and one amino acid
Three fatty acids and one glycerol
questions.explain: A lipid (fat or oil) is made of three fatty acid molecules joined to one glycerol molecule.

questions.q: Why is glucose absorbed from the small intestine into the blood sometimes by active transport?
options: To move water into the blood
Glucose is always at a higher concentration in the gut
To absorb glucose even when its concentration is higher in the blood than the gut
questions.explain: Active transport allows glucose to be absorbed against the gradient when blood glucose is higher than in the gut.

questions.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis eventually level off as light intensity keeps increasing?
options: Another factor such as CO2 or temperature becomes limiting
questions.explain: At high light, another factor (CO2 or temperature) limits the rate, so it plateaus.

questions.q: Each enzyme works on only one type of substrate. This is because:
options: Enzymes only work at one temperature
All enzymes are the same shape
The shape of the active site is complementary to one substrate
questions.explain: The active site has a specific shape that only fits a particular substrate, giving enzymes their specificity.

questions.q: Glucose made in photosynthesis can be converted to which insoluble storage molecule?
questions.explain: Glucose is stored as insoluble starch, which does not affect the cell's water balance.

questions.q: Why does a very high or very low pH usually stop an enzyme working?
options: It turns the enzyme into a product
It changes the shape of the active site, denaturing the enzyme
It gives the enzyme more energy
questions.explain: Extreme pH alters the active site's shape (denaturation) so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: At low light intensity, what is most likely limiting photosynthesis?
questions.explain: When light is in short supply it limits the rate, so increasing light increases photosynthesis.

questions.q: Why are the upper palisade cells, rather than the lower spongy cells, packed with the most chloroplasts?
options: They are nearer the light at the top of the leaf
questions.explain: Palisade cells are at the top of the leaf where light is strongest, so they hold the most chloroplasts.

questions.q: Where does most chemical digestion of food finish?
questions.explain: Enzymes from the pancreas and small intestine complete digestion in the small intestine.

questions.q: In an osmosis investigation, a potato chip GAINED mass. This shows the solution it was in was:
options: The same concentration as the cell contents
More concentrated than the cell contents
More dilute than the cell contents
questions.explain: Gaining mass means water entered by osmosis, so the surrounding solution was more dilute than the cell contents.

questions.q: Why does the stomach produce hydrochloric acid?
options: To provide the optimum pH for stomach protease and kill bacteria
questions.explain: The acidic conditions kill pathogens and give the right pH for the protease in the stomach to work.

questions.q: In which organelle does photosynthesis take place?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll.

questions.q: In the starch test, which colour shows that starch is present?
questions.explain: Iodine solution turns blue-black where starch is present in the leaf.

questions.q: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration speeds up photosynthesis only until...
options: another factor such as light or temperature becomes limiting
questions.explain: CO2 increases the rate until another factor becomes limiting, then the rate levels off.

questions.q: In the emulsion (ethanol) test, a positive result for lipids is:
questions.explain: Adding ethanol then water to a lipid produces a cloudy white emulsion.

questions.q: What happens to a digestive enzyme if the pH is far from its optimum?
options: Its active site changes shape (denatures) and it stops working
It turns into a different enzyme
questions.explain: Extremes of pH denature an enzyme by changing the shape of its active site so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: What is the gas produced by photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Oxygen is released as a product of photosynthesis.

questions.q: A cell placed in a concentrated salt solution loses water and shrinks. This is because water moves:
options: Out of the cell by active transport
Into the cell by diffusion of salt
Out of the cell by osmosis down its water gradient
questions.explain: The salt solution has a lower water concentration, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

questions.q: Light energy in photosynthesis is converted into which form of energy stored in glucose?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

questions.q: When testing a leaf for starch, why is the leaf boiled in ethanol?
options: To soften the cell walls only
To remove the chlorophyll so the colour change is visible
questions.explain: Boiling in ethanol removes chlorophyll, so the iodine colour change can be seen clearly.

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down starch, and into what?
questions.explain: Carbohydrases such as amylase break down starch into simple sugars.

questions.q: Where is bile made?
questions.explain: Bile is produced in the liver and then stored in the gall bladder.
